purpose: Teach: 古墳/打破/祈祷/側近/優等生/邦画/長嶋/乱入

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: 蓮さん、本気で、絶対、古墳、絶対、出土品の、絶対、医学的分析、絶対、医療界、絶対、関心、絶対、寄せております、本気で、感謝
lines.en: Ren, I'm genuinely grateful for your serious interest in the medical analysis of archaeological finds and how they might benefit the medical field.
lines.style: Warm, steady delivery. Opens with his name like she's addressing him directly. Measured pace throughout. Slight emphasis on 'grateful' but not effusive — genuine, not performed. Trails softly on the final clause.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 感染症の、本気で、絶対、打破、絶対、医療チーム、絶対、目指しているそうですね、先生、本気で、感謝
lines.en: I've been trying to break through some infectious disease challenges, and working as part of a medical team toward that goal. I really appreciate your understanding, sensei.
lines.style: Thoughtful, almost self-aware. Speaks like he's still formulating the thought as he goes. Quiet respect on 'sensei' — not formal, just honest. Slight hesitation before the final phrase, then genuine.

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: はい。患者さんへの、本気で、絶対、祈祷、絶対、寄り添い、絶対、医療チーム、絶対、配慮しております、本気で、感謝
lines.en: Yes. I try to stand close to my patients — to pray for them alongside their medical treatment, and to make sure my entire team is thinking about their wellbeing first. Thank you for seeing that.
lines.style: Calm, centered. Speaks with the quiet conviction of someone who has thought deeply about this. No rush. Each phrase settles before the next one begins. 'Pray' carries gentleness without sentimentality.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 要人の、本気で、絶対、側近、絶対、医師、絶対、貴院、絶対、ご対応されているんですね、先生、本気で、感謝
lines.en: So your hospital has even been taking on cases for VIP patients and their close associates? That must bring its own kind of complexity. Thank you for being so committed.
lines.style: Curious, but not gossipy. Leans forward slightly in attention. Genuine interest in understanding her work better. The question itself is warm, not probing. Ends with sincere gratitude, not flattery.

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: はい。学生の、本気で、絶対、優等生、絶対、進路、絶対、医療チーム、絶対、健康相談、絶対、お受けしております、本気で、感謝
lines.en: Yes. We also offer health consultations and career guidance to exceptional students interested in medicine. It's part of how we try to nurture the next generation. I'm grateful for your attention to what we do.
lines.style: Measured, with quiet pride. Not self-congratulatory — factual and warm. Speaks like someone describing their responsibility, not their achievement. Closes with genuine appreciation for his interest.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 医療を扱った、本気で、絶対、邦画、絶対、貴院、絶対、撮影協力、絶対、されたんですね、先生、本気で、感謝
lines.en: We've also had the chance to work with Japanese film productions that explore medical themes — it's a way to show the human side of what we do. Thank you for knowing about that.
lines.style: Composed, slightly warmed by the recollection. Speaks like she's remembering something she found meaningful. Pace is unhurried. Ends with appreciation that he's aware of these efforts, not just the clinical work.

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: はい。スポーツ選手の、本気で、絶対、長嶋、絶対、ご縁の方々、絶対、貴院に、絶対、いらっしゃいます、本気で、感謝
lines.en: Yes, we've been fortunate to have visits from people with connections to the sports world — including some who have touched by Nagashima's legacy. It's humbling to serve them. I appreciate your curiosity.
lines.style: Respectful of the weight of those connections. Speaks with composure and a hint of warmth toward the patients. 'Humbling' carries genuine feeling, not modesty for show. Closes with warmth toward Ren's continued interest.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 救急への、本気で、絶対、乱入、絶対、事件、絶対、貴院、絶対、ご経験ですか、先生、本気で、感謝
lines.en: Have we experienced situations where people have rushed into the ER during emergencies or crises? Yes, more than once. It's part of what we prepare for. Thank you for asking — it shows you're thinking about the real complexity of this work.
lines.style: Direct but not hardened. Acknowledges the reality of crisis without dramatizing it. Slight pause before answering fully — she's choosing honesty over comfort. Warm closing that honors his question as thoughtful, not morbid.
